title: The Milky Way over Cerro Armazones
caption: The Milky Way over the Astronomical Site Monitor on Cerro Armazones, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at the ELT site, Cerro Armazones, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: At night on Cerro Armazones in Chile's Atacama Desert, the Milky Way stretches across the sky above ESO's Astronomical Site Monitor. Our galaxy's disc is seen edge-on, and to the left of the tall tower its centre appears as a yellow bulge scored with dark lanes.

Those dark lanes are nebulae, where cosmic dust blocks the light behind. In ancient Andean cosmology they formed constellations of their own. One of them, the llama, extends rightward from a point above the tower, and its eye is the bright star Alpha Centauri.

Cerro Armazones lies about 20 km from Cerro Paranal and ESO's Very Large Telescope, and it is the chosen site for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). Monitoring equipment like the one pictured helps characterise the conditions a site offers. ESO Photo Ambassador Serge Brunier took this photograph.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based night photograph by Serge Brunier. The source does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the yellow bulge and dark lanes may look more pronounced here than to someone on the mountain.
